claims.text: The driver's own trace never places him inside the pickup geofence. The derived arrival block reports qualifying_fix_count 0 and a longest qualifying run of 0 seconds against the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and the 25 m accuracy filter, so there is no qualifying in-radius fix anywhere in the 15 minutes preceding the 08:20:30 cancellation. Under POL-NS-02 that means the driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee.

The required dwell is 300 seconds for a STANDARD pickup and the driver's longest qualifying in-geofence run is 0.0 seconds. The clock runs from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the driver's 'arrived' tap at 08:12:35, so the 7.9 minutes of wall time in the trip record is not dwell. POL-NS-01 limb (c) fails on this arithmetic alone, independently of limb (b).

Stated as the numbers POL-NS-06 asks for: minimum dwell 300 s, measured in-geofence dwell 0 s, shortfall 300 s. POL-NS-06 makes a dwell shorter than the minimum non-chargeable, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages, so the cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.00 itemised in the fare breakdown must be refunded in full.

The driver cannot close that shortfall by accumulating separate in-geofence intervals or by pleading a kerbside restriction. POL-NS-06(i) permits accumulation only where a present and populated traffic_advisory of an admissible type covers the pickup road and the waiting period, and EV-ADVIS-00212-01 is MISSING with a null payload. A MISSING artifact carries weight 0.0 and can support no fact, so limb (i) is unavailable and the 300 second shortfall stands.

This is not a wrong-entrance case under POL-NS-03. That route requires the driver to have been stationary for the required dwell within 400 m of the pin; his own track shows motion at distinct speeds of 25.2 and 43.5 km/h inside the waiting window, a mean distance of 294 m from the pin, and zero stationary in-geofence interval. With no qualifying stationary dwell anywhere, POL-NS-03 does not apply and the outcome is governed by POL-NS-02.

The driver's account that he was 'parked at the kerb outside Exit A for nearly eight minutes' is contradicted by his own trace: 3.2 km travelled, a maximum of 1082 m from the pickup pin, speeds of 25.2 and 43.5 km/h, and no qualifying in-geofence fix at any point. On those facts the 08:12:35 'arrived' marker did not start a genuine kerbside wait under POL-NS-05, and because there is no qualifying in-geofence fix anywhere in the trip, limb (ii) directs a full refund and a false-arrival entry against the driver.

The driver's suggestion that the rider may have been on the wrong side is the POL-NS-03 frame, and it fails on the rider's side too. Her track carries 60 fixes with a mean distance of 22.6 m and a maximum of 40.4 m from the pin, so she was at the pickup and not elsewhere, and at 08:15:02 she messaged 'im at exit A, which car ah? i dont see anything here' with no indication of moving afterwards. The failure to complete this pickup is at the driver's end.

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 compensates the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; POL-NS-01 fails at limbs (b) and (c), and POL-NS-06 independently displaces the charge by reason of the 300 second shortfall. The rider should not fund a trip on which the driver never reached the pickup point.

claims.text: The trip_record terminates this trip by the driver at 08:20:30 with cancellation_reason_code EXCESSIVE_WAIT and records no boarding event, which is precisely the limb (d) condition POL-NS-01 recognises; the driver entered one of the three truthful codes the clause names rather than the self-defeating DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, so the termination is a genuine no-show termination and not an admission that he could not find the rider.

POL-NS-01 limb (a) is satisfied: the trip_record carries a driver 'arrived' event for TRP-00212 at 08:12:35, and the driver's own trace runs without interruption from its first fix at 08:05:10 to the cancellation at 08:20:30, so this was a worked pickup attempt started on a real arrival marker rather than a bare app tap.

On the driver's own trace the car comes within 37.94 m of the pickup pin, that is inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD zone, and the derived arrival block reports a qualifying-fix count of 0 only because that in-radius fix did not survive the 25 m accuracy filter; POL-NS-02 provides that accuracy-filtered fixes 'count as evidence of neither presence nor absence', so the trace cannot be read as a driver who abandoned the pickup - it is an accuracy-limited reading of a driver who was at the pickup area of the venue, which is the wrong-face situation POL-NS-02 hands to POL-NS-03.

POL-NS-04 does not apply on this chat: the rider's locating message sent at 08:15:02 was answered by the driver 28 seconds later at 08:15:30, inside the 120 second window required by limb (b), so the rider is not exonerated by this clause and no refund follows from it regardless of the content of the reply.

The POL-NS-05 false-arrival trigger is not made out on this record: the clause turns on matching the arrival marker at 08:12:35 to the GPS fix nearest that timestamp and showing the driver more than 300 m from the pin or travelling at 15 km/h or more, and the derived arrival block publishes no arrival-matched fix and leaves dwell_start_offset_sec null, so the driver's arrival marker stands unrebutted and the fee cannot be struck down on this clause.

Whatever went wrong at the pickup, it was a location mismatch and not an abandonment: the driver's trace is continuous across the entire 15 minute 20 second window (100 percent coverage, 93 fixes at a 10 second cadence, no gaps, maximum gap 0 seconds) and averages 294.05 m from the pin, inside the 400 m corridor POL-NS-03 uses to separate a driver at the wrong face of the venue from one who drove off to another job.

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip and must not be used to escalate this case: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the absolute threshold of 4, and 2 terminations over driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 132 is a rate of 0.015, below the 0.08 threshold, so POL-NS-09(d) is not engaged; on a fee that stands the driver's entitlement would be 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee, SGD 3.20.

There is no fare-integrity defect for either side to trade on: POL-NS-01's resolution rule takes the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), so the SGD 4.00 cancellation-fee line in the ledger reconciles with the schedule and POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged, leaving the amount itself unquestioned.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full.

For the rider: your core point is upheld. Under POL-NS-02 the driver is deemed to have arrived only if the GPS trace carries at least three consecutive fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at 25 m accuracy or better. The driver's own trace (EV-GPS-00212) reports qualifying_fix_count 0 and a longest qualifying in-geofence run of 0.0 s across the fifteen minutes before the 08:20:30 cancellation. His closest approach was 37.94 m from the pin, i.e. inside the 50 m radius, but that fix did not clear the 25 m accuracy filter, and POL-NS-02 provides that accuracy-filtered fixes count as evidence of neither presence nor absence. With no qualifying in-radius fix anywhere in the window, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails and the fee is not chargeable. The waiting-period arithmetic is the same story: the required dwell for a STANDARD pickup is 300 s (POL-NS-01 limb (c); POL-NS-06), the measured in-geofence dwell is 0 s and the shortfall is 300 s, so POL-NS-06 makes the fee non-chargeable whether or not you were present. The fare line refunded is the cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.00 in fare_breakdown (total_charged SGD 4.00, payment_status CHARGED, nothing yet refunded).

For the driver: your claims that POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are met are accepted (the trip record carries an 'arrived' event at 08:12:35 and terminates by you with EXCESSIVE_WAIT, not DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE), as is your point that the anti-farming check does not trip and that the fare reconciles. But the clause is conjunctive and fails at (b) and (c), and two of your arguments do not move the outcome. POL-NS-03 does not govern: it applies only where the trace shows you stationary for the required dwell within 400 m of the pin, and your own trace shows movement across the window - 3.2 km travelled, speeds of 25.2 and 43.5 km/h, and a maximum distance of 1082 m from the pin - so a mean distance of 294.05 m does not establish a parked position inside the 400 m corridor. Even if it did, POL-NS-03 would still refund the fee and would award you nothing, because the rider named Exit A in the chat log (POL-NS-03(i)) and registered_pickup_points is 1, so the pin-ambiguity goodwill route (POL-NS-03(ii), needing 2 or more) is unavailable. Driver compensation is therefore nil: POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, and that is not this case. The 80% figure of SGD 3.20 you cite is simply never reached, and POL-NS-09(d) is not engaged (2 terminations, below 4; 2/132 = 0.015, below 0.08).

On the contested rider claim that the 08:12:35 marker is a FALSE arrival under POL-NS-05 and that limb (ii) should record a false-arrival event against the driver: that is not made out. POL-NS-05 turns on a single GPS fix matched to the arrival timestamp showing the driver more than 300 m from the pin, or travelling at 15 km/h or above; the derived trace publishes no arrival-matched fix and leaves dwell_start_offset_sec null, so the test cannot be run on this record. The refund follows from POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06, not from POL-NS-05, and no false-arrival referral issues.

Other matters: POL-NS-04 does not apply, because the rider's locating message at 08:15:02 was answered by the driver at 08:15:30, inside the 120 s window. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00212-01 is MISSING, with a null payload and weight 0.0; its absence is citable but it can carry no fact, so POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is unavailable and the 300 s shortfall stands unreduced.

No escalation. Confidence is 0.85, above the 0.70 floor. No POL-NS-08(a)-(d) impairment: there is no clock skew (the 08:12:35 arrival sits within 5 s of a fix on the 10 s cadence, and acceptance and termination times match), no trace gap (93 fixes, maximum gap 0.0 s) and the rider track is present, the chat log holds all four messages in sequence with no five-minute gap, and the SGD 4.00 fee reconciles with the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) under POL-NS-01's resolution rule, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged. No repeat-dispute pattern exists (both disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0). The confidence cap is 1.0 - the GPS trace at weight 1.0 is the sole carrier of the deciding fact - so 0.85 sits below the cap.

To both parties: the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee (EV-FARE-00212, cancellation_fee line) is refunded to the rider in full, and no driver compensation is payable.

Why the fee cannot stand. POL-NS-01 lets a no-show fee stand only if all four limbs hold, and limbs (b) and (c) do not. The driver's own trace (EV-GPS-00212) covers the whole waiting window - 93 fixes at 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps - but against the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and the 25 m accuracy filter it records 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes and a longest qualifying in-geofence run of 0 seconds. POL-NS-02 says fixes worse than 25 m accuracy count as evidence of neither presence nor absence, so the trace cannot establish an admissible arrival: no qualifying in-radius fix anywhere in the 15 minutes before the 08:20:30 cancellation means the driver never arrived and limb (b) fails, with a full refund. Independently, the waiting clock runs from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from the 08:12:35 'arrived' tap (POL-NS-01 limb (c)), so measured dwell is 0 s against the 300 s minimum - a 300 s shortfall - and POL-NS-06 makes the fee non-chargeable and refundable in full whether or not the rider was present. The 7.9 minutes of app wall-time is not dwell.

Driver: your account of being parked at the kerb for nearly eight minutes is not carried by any admissible fix. Your trace shows 3.2 km travelled, a maximum 1082 m from the pin, speeds of 25.2 and 43.5 km/h and no stationary in-geofence interval. Your point that a raw fix came within 37.94 m of the pin does not help: it did not survive the 25 m accuracy filter and counts as evidence of neither presence nor absence. Limb (d) is indeed satisfied - EXCESSIVE_WAIT is one of the three codes POL-NS-01 recognises - but one limb of four does not carry the fee. Your POL-NS-03 wrong-entrance route produces no compensation either: it requires you to have been stationary for the required dwell within 400 m of the pin, which is not shown (and a mean distance of 294 m inside the 400 m corridor is not the test), and in any event registered_pickup_points is 1 and the rider named Exit A in chat, so the pin-ambiguity goodwill limb (ii) cannot apply and limb (i) awards you nothing. POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, so compensation is nil. For completeness, the anti-farming check does not trip (2 no-show terminations in 30 days, below the absolute threshold of 4, and a rate of 0.015 across 132 completed trips, below 0.08), so POL-NS-09(d) and escalation are not engaged.

Rider: your presence at the pin (your track averages 22.6 m and peaks at 40.4 m from it) is confirmed but is not what decides this - POL-NS-06 refunds regardless of rider presence, and POL-NS-04 does not separately exonerate you because the driver answered your 08:15:02 message 28 seconds later, inside its 120-second window.

On the requested false-arrival record under POL-NS-05(ii): POL-NS-05 fires only where the GPS places the driver more than 300 m from the pin, or moving at 15 km/h or more, at the 08:12:35 arrival-marker timestamp. The computed trace publishes no arrival-matched fix, and a whole-window maximum distance cannot establish the position at the marker, so the false-arrival trigger is not made out and I record no referral on that clause. The refund does not depend on it.

On integrity and confidence. No artifact is impaired for policy purposes under POL-NS-08(a)-(d): the event and trace timestamps agree to the second, the trace has no gap above 120 s and includes the rider's track, the chat log's four messages match chat_message_count 4 with no missing msg_id, and the SGD 4.00 fee reconciles with the fee_schedule resolution rule - the greater of the SGD 4.00 STANDARD zone-class fee and the SGD 4.00 RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00212-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0), so POL-NS-06(i) accumulation was never available, but nothing turned on it, and citing the missing artifact to establish its own unavailability does not trigger POL-NS-09. Every artifact this ruling rests on carries weight 1.0, so confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor. No profile field outside those the policy names was used as a ground.

To both parties: the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is refunded in full to the rider, and no compensation is payable to the driver.

Why the fee cannot stand. POL-NS-01 charges a no-show fee only if all four limbs hold. Limb (a) holds (the trip record carries an 'arrived' event at 08:12:35) and limb (d) holds (the trip was terminated by the driver at 08:20:30 under EXCESSIVE_WAIT with no boarding event). Limbs (b) and (c) fail. Limb (b) is the POL-NS-02 test: the GPS trace must contain at least three consecutive fixes, each accurate to 25 m or better, within the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD pickup. EV-GPS-00212 reports qualifying_fix_count 0 and a longest qualifying in-radius run of 0.0 seconds across the whole 08:05:10-08:20:30 trace (100% coverage, 93 fixes, no gaps). The closest recorded approach is 37.94 m, but that fix did not survive the 25 m accuracy filter, and POL-NS-02 provides that filtered fixes count as evidence of neither presence nor absence. With no qualifying in-radius fix at any point in the 15 minutes before the 08:20:30 cancellation, the driver never arrived and limb (b) fails. Limb (c) fails independently: the required dwell for STANDARD is 300 seconds measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, and that figure is 0 seconds - a shortfall of 300 seconds - so POL-NS-06 makes the fee non-chargeable and refundable in full whether or not the rider was present or responsive. The trip record's 7.9 minutes of 'wait time' is simply the interval from the driver's own arrived tap to his cancellation; POL-NS-01(c) measures the clock from GPS entry into the geofence, not from the tap.

The driver's account that he was 'parked at the kerb outside Exit A for nearly eight minutes' is contradicted by his own trace: 3.2 km travelled, a maximum of 1,082 m from the pin, and speeds of 25.2 and 43.5 km/h. POL-NS-03 (wrong-entrance) does not apply because it requires the driver to have been stationary for the required dwell within 400 m of the pin, and no such stationary in-geofence interval exists; his average distance of 294 m shows movement, not a hold. The claim for compensation under POL-NS-07 is refused: that clause pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; POL-NS-01 fails at (b) and (c) and POL-NS-06 displaces the charge. POL-NS-03(ii) goodwill does not arise either, and in any event registered_pickup_points is 1, not 2 or more.

The rider's further claim that POL-NS-05's false-arrival trigger fires, entitling her to a false-arrival entry against the driver, is not accepted. That clause turns on matching the 08:12:35 'arrived' event to the GPS fix nearest that timestamp and showing the driver more than 300 m from the pin or travelling at 15 km/h or above; the derived record publishes no such arrival-matched fix, and the mean distance of 294 m sits inside the 300 m leash. The refund therefore rests on POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06, not on POL-NS-05, and no referral is produced. Her exoneration claim under POL-NS-04 equally does not carry the case: the driver replied to her 08:15:02 message at 08:15:30, 28 seconds later and inside the 120 second window, so that clause does not apply - she nevertheless wins on the GPS arithmetic alone.

On integrity: POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged - the SGD 4.00 cancellation-fee line equals the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) under the fee schedule. There is no clock skew beyond 90 seconds, no sampling gap over 120 seconds, and no chat defect (4 messages against a recorded count of 4). EV-ADVIS-00212-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0) and can support no fact; its absence makes the POL-NS-06(i) accumulation route unavailable, but nothing turns on it because the 300 second shortfall is not cured by any advisory. No escalation arises under POL-NS-09: the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (2 no-show terminations in 30 days against a threshold of 4, and a rate of 0.015 against 0.08), no clause leaves a contradiction on arrival or dwell unresolved, and confidence is above the platform floor of 0.70. The parties' profile fields were treated as context only under POL-GEN-01. Every figure used above is read off the trip record, GPS derived block and fare breakdown in the brief.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full, and the driver receives no compensation.

Why the fee cannot stand. A no-show fee is chargeable only if all four POL-NS-01 conditions hold, and the driver's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-00212, weight 1.0, no integrity flags) fails two of them. Limb (b): under POL-NS-02 the driver is deemed 'arrived' only where the trace contains at least three consecutive fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius that pass the 25 m accuracy filter; the computed arrival block returns qualifying_fix_count 0 and a longest qualifying run of 0 s, so no qualifying in-radius fix exists anywhere in the 15 minutes before the 08:20:30 cancellation. The nearest reading was 37.94 m, but it does not survive the accuracy filter, and POL-NS-02 provides that such fixes count as evidence of neither presence nor absence. Limb (c): POL-NS-01 measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the 08:12:35 'arrived' tap, and the longest qualifying in-geofence run is 0 s against the required 300 s for a STANDARD pickup. POL-NS-06 states the same arithmetic - required 300 s, measured 0 s, shortfall 300 s - and makes the cancellation-fee line refundable whether or not the rider was present or responsive. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00212-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, payload null), so POL-NS-06(i) accumulation across separate in-geofence intervals is unavailable and the 300 s shortfall stands; the clause tells us a MISSING advisory triggers POL-NS-09 rather than exonerating anyone, and nothing here is asserted against it.

The driver's account of being 'parked at the kerb outside Exit A for nearly eight minutes' is contradicted by his own trace: over the 15 min 20 s window the car covered 3.2 km, reached 1082 m from the pin, showed speeds of 25.2 and 43.5 km/h, and recorded no stationary in-geofence interval. POL-NS-03 (wrong-face-of-venue) does not apply, because it requires a stationary hold of the required dwell within 400 m of the pin and the trace shows movement rather than a hold. Even if it applied it would also refund the fee in full, and because the rider named the correct entrance in chat ('im at exit A'), the fault would fall on the driver and no compensation would follow (registered_pickup_points is 1, so the pin-ambiguity goodwill route does not open either). The rider's own trace (60 fixes, mean 22.6 m, maximum 40.4 m from the pin) confirms she was at the pickup point, and her 08:15:02 message was answered by the driver 28 seconds later at 08:15:30, so POL-NS-04 does not exonerate her and produces no refund on that route.

On the driver's POL-NS-01 claims: limbs (a) and (d) are accepted - the trip record does carry an 'arrived' event at 08:12:35 and does terminate the trip by the driver with reason code EXCESSIVE_WAIT and no boarding event - but a fee needs all four limbs, and (b) and (c) fail. The submission that the 37.94 m reading is merely an accuracy-limited view of a driver at the pickup is rejected: POL-NS-02 expressly treats accuracy-filtered fixes as proving neither presence nor absence, and POL-NS-03 still requires a stationary dwell the trace does not show. On POL-NS-05, both sides' positions are answered together: the clause's trigger needs the fix at the 08:12:35 arrival marker to place the driver more than 300 m out or travelling at 15 km/h or more, and the computed arrival block publishes no arrival-matched fix and leaves dwell_start_offset_sec null, so that trigger is not established on this record. The rider's request for a false-arrival referral is therefore declined, and equally the driver's arrival marker cannot be confirmed as genuine - the marker does not start a validated waiting clock either way.

No driver compensation. POL-NS-07 pays the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; limbs (b) and (c) fail and POL-NS-06 displaces the charge, so nothing is payable. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check is not reached (2 no-show terminations against 132 completed trips, a rate of 0.015, below both the count of 4 and the rate of 0.08), so POL-NS-09(d) is not engaged and the rider should not be left funding a trip on which the driver never reached the pickup point.

No escalation. The bundle is clean - 100% GPS coverage, no sampling gap (max gap 0 s), 93 driver and 60 rider fixes, 4 chat messages matching the trip record's chat count, and a SGD 4.00 fee line that reconciles with the fee schedule (the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee 4.00). No limb (a) to (d) of POL-NS-08 fires, confidence is above the 0.70 floor, and no direct artifact contradiction on arrival, dwell or rider presence is left unresolved by a clause.

Amount: the SGD 4.00 refunded is the cancellation_fee line of EV-FARE-00212 (total_charged 4.00), returned in full.

ledger.claim: The driver's own trace never places him inside the pickup geofence. The derived arrival block reports qualifying_fix_count 0 and a longest qualifying run of 0 seconds against the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and the 25 m accuracy filter, so there is no qualifying in-radius fix anywhere in the 15 minutes preceding the 08:20:30 cancellation. Under POL-NS-02 that means the driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee.

The required dwell is 300 seconds for a STANDARD pickup and the driver's longest qualifying in-geofence run is 0.0 seconds. The clock runs from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the driver's 'arrived' tap at 08:12:35, so the 7.9 minutes of wall time in the trip record is not dwell. POL-NS-01 limb (c) fails on this arithmetic alone, independently of limb (b).

Stated as the numbers POL-NS-06 asks for: minimum dwell 300 s, measured in-geofence dwell 0 s, shortfall 300 s. POL-NS-06 makes a dwell shorter than the minimum non-chargeable, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages, so the cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.00 itemised in the fare breakdown must be refunded in full.

The driver cannot close that shortfall by accumulating separate in-geofence intervals or by pleading a kerbside restriction. POL-NS-06(i) permits accumulation only where a present and populated traffic_advisory of an admissible type covers the pickup road and the waiting period, and EV-ADVIS-00212-01 is MISSING with a null payload. A MISSING artifact carries weight 0.0 and can support no fact, so limb (i) is unavailable and the 300 second shortfall stands.

This is not a wrong-entrance case under POL-NS-03. That route requires the driver to have been stationary for the required dwell within 400 m of the pin; his own track shows motion at distinct speeds of 25.2 and 43.5 km/h inside the waiting window, a mean distance of 294 m from the pin, and zero stationary in-geofence interval. With no qualifying stationary dwell anywhere, POL-NS-03 does not apply and the outcome is governed by POL-NS-02.

The driver's account that he was 'parked at the kerb outside Exit A for nearly eight minutes' is contradicted by his own trace: 3.2 km travelled, a maximum of 1082 m from the pickup pin, speeds of 25.2 and 43.5 km/h, and no qualifying in-geofence fix at any point. On those facts the 08:12:35 'arrived' marker did not start a genuine kerbside wait under POL-NS-05, and because there is no qualifying in-geofence fix anywhere in the trip, limb (ii) directs a full refund and a false-arrival entry against the driver.

The driver's suggestion that the rider may have been on the wrong side is the POL-NS-03 frame, and it fails on the rider's side too. Her track carries 60 fixes with a mean distance of 22.6 m and a maximum of 40.4 m from the pin, so she was at the pickup and not elsewhere, and at 08:15:02 she messaged 'im at exit A, which car ah? i dont see anything here' with no indication of moving afterwards. The failure to complete this pickup is at the driver's end.

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 compensates the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; POL-NS-01 fails at limbs (b) and (c), and POL-NS-06 independently displaces the charge by reason of the 300 second shortfall. The rider should not fund a trip on which the driver never reached the pickup point.

The trip_record terminates this trip by the driver at 08:20:30 with cancellation_reason_code EXCESSIVE_WAIT and records no boarding event, which is precisely the limb (d) condition POL-NS-01 recognises; the driver entered one of the three truthful codes the clause names rather than the self-defeating DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, so the termination is a genuine no-show termination and not an admission that he could not find the rider.

POL-NS-01 limb (a) is satisfied: the trip_record carries a driver 'arrived' event for TRP-00212 at 08:12:35, and the driver's own trace runs without interruption from its first fix at 08:05:10 to the cancellation at 08:20:30, so this was a worked pickup attempt started on a real arrival marker rather than a bare app tap.

On the driver's own trace the car comes within 37.94 m of the pickup pin, that is inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD zone, and the derived arrival block reports a qualifying-fix count of 0 only because that in-radius fix did not survive the 25 m accuracy filter; POL-NS-02 provides that accuracy-filtered fixes 'count as evidence of neither presence nor absence', so the trace cannot be read as a driver who abandoned the pickup - it is an accuracy-limited reading of a driver who was at the pickup area of the venue, which is the wrong-face situation POL-NS-02 hands to POL-NS-03.

POL-NS-04 does not apply on this chat: the rider's locating message sent at 08:15:02 was answered by the driver 28 seconds later at 08:15:30, inside the 120 second window required by limb (b), so the rider is not exonerated by this clause and no refund follows from it regardless of the content of the reply.

The POL-NS-05 false-arrival trigger is not made out on this record: the clause turns on matching the arrival marker at 08:12:35 to the GPS fix nearest that timestamp and showing the driver more than 300 m from the pin or travelling at 15 km/h or more, and the derived arrival block publishes no arrival-matched fix and leaves dwell_start_offset_sec null, so the driver's arrival marker stands unrebutted and the fee cannot be struck down on this clause.

Whatever went wrong at the pickup, it was a location mismatch and not an abandonment: the driver's trace is continuous across the entire 15 minute 20 second window (100 percent coverage, 93 fixes at a 10 second cadence, no gaps, maximum gap 0 seconds) and averages 294.05 m from the pin, inside the 400 m corridor POL-NS-03 uses to separate a driver at the wrong face of the venue from one who drove off to another job.

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip and must not be used to escalate this case: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the absolute threshold of 4, and 2 terminations over driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 132 is a rate of 0.015, below the 0.08 threshold, so POL-NS-09(d) is not engaged; on a fee that stands the driver's entitlement would be 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee, SGD 3.20.

There is no fare-integrity defect for either side to trade on: POL-NS-01's resolution rule takes the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), so the SGD 4.00 cancellation-fee line in the ledger reconciles with the schedule and POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged, leaving the amount itself unquestioned.
